scenario: [LCST.4.5.11]: a `Json` leaf takes [LCST.4.5.2]'s row for the kind it holds when the conversion runs. One fact per case, each matched by its own rule on `k`: `a`'s Float leaf `31.7` under `::Int?` is 31, the Float row to `Int`; `b`'s String leaf `"31.5"` under `::Float?` parses as a `String` does, 31.5; `c`'s String leaf `"abc"` under `::Float?` does not parse, so the fallible row gives `null`; `d`'s absent path reads `null` ([LNUL.8.4]), and the cast gives `null` ([LCST.4.2.3]). Each rule logs, in source order: ["float to int", "string parses", "string does not parse", "absent"]. A runtime that read a leaf by one fixed kind fails at least one. PATH PINNED: `dsc.rete.lcst_4_5_11_dispatch`'s `is_float`, `is_string` and `is_null` arms, through `FN_FLOAT_TO_INT` and `FN_STRING_TO_FLOAT`, in each runtime.
rules_ds:
schema Doc scope logical:
    k: String key
    body: Json mutable

rule float_to_int:
    Doc d where d.k == "a" and d.body.c::Int? == 31
->
    log info "float to int"

rule string_parses:
    Doc d where d.k == "b" and d.body.c::Float? == 31.5
->
    log info "string parses"

rule string_does_not_parse:
    Doc d where d.k == "c" and d.body.c::Float? is null
->
    log info "string does not parse"

rule absent:
    Doc d where d.k == "d" and d.body.c::Float? is null
->
    log info "absent"
